title: SharePoint: new SharePoint experience with Discover, Publish and Build in a redesigned app bar
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing distinctions and documented controls are supported. Two admin paths stop early in the correct place and should include the final documented choice.

claims.claim: Extra restrictions might apply to My News in GCC High and DoD.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Specific SharePoint app bar tabs cannot be disabled.
claims.quote: Specific SharePoint app bar tabs can't be disabled.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The app bar cannot be disabled on specific sites.
claims.quote: The SharePoint app bar can't be disabled on specific sites.

claims.claim: Control site creation from tools governs creation from SharePoint, OneDrive, PnP PowerShell and REST.
claims.quote: This setting controls whether users can create sites from SharePoint, OneDrive, the PnP PowerShell cmdlet, and the REST API.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling SharePoint site creation does not prevent Microsoft 365 group creation or group-dependent resources such as Teams.
claims.quote: Disabling site creation for users doesn't remove their ability to create Microsoft 365 groups or resources, such as Microsoft Teams, that rely on a group.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The existing self-service site creation control applies to creating sites from Build.
claims.quote: Users must be allowed to create SharePoint sites in your organization. To enable users create new sites, admins must enable self-service site creation.

claims.claim: SharePoint Administrators and above can manage site creation settings.
claims.quote: As a SharePoint Administrator and above in Microsoft 365, you can let your users create and manage their own SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant requires a SharePoint Online administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.claim: Site creation is controlled in SharePoint admin center > Settings > Site creation > Control site creation from tools.
claims.quote: Go to Settings in the SharePoint admin center ... Select Site creation. ... To allow users to create sites, select Allow under Control site creation from tools.
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path to 'Settings > Site creation > Control site creation from tools > Allow', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/manage-site-creation. Keep the note describing the setting's scope.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -SelfServiceSiteCreationDisabled $true disables self-service site creation.
claims.quote: -SelfServiceSiteCreationDisabled: When set to True, users cannot create sites from SharePoint, OneDrive, the PnP PowerShell cmdlet, and the REST API. PARAMVALUE: True | False

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for controlling SPFx placeholder placement relative to elevated content.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint DisableSpfxTopBottomPlaceholdersInElevatedContent admin center setting'; opened Set-SPOTenant, New SharePoint Experience and the app bar page. The reference documents the PowerShell parameter; no admin UI was found.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -DisableSpfxTopBottomPlaceholdersInElevatedContent $true controls SPFx top and bottom placeholder placement.
claims.quote: -DisableSpfxTopBottomPlaceholdersInElevatedContent ... This feature allows SharePoint Administrators to control where SPFx Top and Bottom placeholders are rendered in relation to elevated content. PARAMVALUE: True | False

claims.claim: True renders the SPFx top and bottom placeholders outside the elevated content area.
claims.quote: Accepts a value of true to render the Top and Bottom placeholders outside the elevated content area

claims.claim: False renders the SPFx top and bottom placeholders inside the elevated content area.
claims.quote: or false to render them inside the elevated content area.

claims.claim: DisableSpfxTopBottomPlaceholdersInElevatedContent defaults to false.
claims.quote: By default, this feature is set to false.

claims.claim: A SharePoint home site is a communication site designated as a home site.
claims.quote: A home site is a communication site that you create and set as the top landing page for all users in your intranet.

claims.claim: A home site is needed to enable and customise global navigation.
claims.quote: You need a home site to enable and customize global navigation in the SharePoint app bar.

claims.claim: Home sites can be managed at SharePoint admin center > Settings > Home sites > Add.
claims.quote: Select Settings, and then select Home sites. ... Option 2: Use an existing communication site ... Select Add, and then select Use an existing communication site.
claims.fix: Extend controls[4].ui.path to 'Settings > Home sites > Add > Use an existing communication site', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/homesites/set-up-admin-center. This preserves the row's purpose of designating an existing communication site.

claims.claim: Set-SPOHomeSite -HomeSiteUrl <home site URL> designates a SharePoint home site.
claims.quote: Module: Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell Module. Sets a SharePoint Site as a Home Site. Set-SPOHomeSite -HomeSiteUrl <String>

claims.claim: Managing home sites in SharePoint admin center requires SharePoint admin or higher.
claims.quote: Sign in to the SharePoint admin center as a SharePoint admin or higher.

claims.claim: Global navigation is enabled on the SharePoint home site at Settings > Global navigation > Enable global navigation.
claims.quote: Go to your organization’s SharePoint home site. Select Settings and then select Global navigation settings. ... Switch the Enable global navigation toggle to On.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API or PowerShell operation for the Enable global navigation toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint global navigation enable PowerShell API app bar disable tabs Publish Build' and 'SharePoint app bar global navigation Graph PowerShell enable toggle'; opened app bar documentation and searched Set-SPOTenant for GlobalNavigation. No operation for this toggle found.

claims.claim: Enabling global navigation requires site owner permissions or higher on the home site.
claims.quote: To enable global navigation, you need site owner permissions (or higher) to the SharePoint home site.

claims.claim: Users need read access or higher to the home site to view its global navigation links.
claims.quote: To view the global navigation links, users need read access (or higher) to the SharePoint home site.

claims.claim: Global navigation changes might take up to 24 hours to reach users.
claims.quote: After implementing global navigation, it might take up to 24 hours for the changes to take effect for users.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant UI or automation setting to turn off or defer the new experience is documented in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'new SharePoint experience disable defer opt out default automatic Set-SPOTenant'; opened New SharePoint Experience and app bar documentation; searched Set-SPOTenant for NewSharePoint, NewExperience and AppBar. No current switch documented; forum preview claims are not product documentation.

claims.claim: No UI or automation control to hide individual Publish or Build app bar tabs is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint global navigation enable PowerShell API app bar disable tabs Publish Build'; opened Introduction to the SharePoint app bar and searched Set-SPOTenant for AppBar. The app bar page expressly says specific tabs cannot be disabled.

claims.claim: Global navigation is configured in the home site's settings rather than in an admin centre.
claims.quote: Go to your organization’s SharePoint home site. Select Settings and then select Global navigation settings.

claims.claim: Restricting site creation does not hide the Publish and Build app bar tabs.
claims.quote: The SharePoint app bar brings together intranet resources and quick access to Discover, Publish, Build, and OneDrive. ... Specific SharePoint app bar tabs can't be disabled.
